text: The laboratory results indicate a low red blood cell (RBC) count of 3.8 million cells per µL and a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 75 fL. An MCV below the normal range (typically 80–100 fL) signifies microcytosis, meaning the red blood cells are smaller than usual. Combined with the low RBC count, this presentation is consistent with microcytic anemia. The most common cause of microcytic anemia is iron deficiency, so further evaluation with iron studies (such as serum ferritin, iron, TIBC, and transferrin saturation) is recommended to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.
